name: Kumar Birla
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (1997-2025); Hurun Global (2014-2026); Hurun India (2016-2022); Wikidata (2019)
forbes_bio: Commodities king Kumar Birla is the fourth generation head of the storied, $67 billion (revenue) Aditya Birla Group. Nearly half is generated outside India, where it has a presence in 40 countries.
The group's interests span cement, textiles and aluminium to telecom, financial services and paints. It has recently entered new sectors such as branded jewellery and hospitality.
Birla, who is a chartered accountant and graduated from London Business School, inherited the family empire at age 28 when his father Aditya Birla died in 1995.
In 2021, he stepped down as chairman of  debt-strapped telecom firm Vodafone Idea, formed by the 2018 merger between his Idea Cellular and Vodafone India.
In 2023, his daughter Ananya and son Aryaman joined the boards of Grasim and Aditya Birla Fashion and Retail.
forbes_facts: The Birla empire's roots go back to 1857 in cotton trading in Rajasthan state.
Daughter Ananya has founded a micro finance firm and an online venture to sell luxury, handmade products.
In 2023, he was conferred the Padma Bhushan, one of India's highest civilian honours.

name: Zhu Yi
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2001-2025); Hurun Global (2023-2026); Hurun China (2023-2026)
forbes_bio: Zhu Yi is the chairman of Biokin Pharmaceutical, a developer of drugs including anesthesia injections, cancer drugs as well as traditional Chinese medicine treatments.
The company went public in Shanghai in 2023, raising $136 million; it has been seeking a Hong Kong IPO since 2024.
Biokin's U.S. subsidiary SystImmune signed in 2023 an $8.4 billion deal with Bristol Myers Squibb to jointly develop and commercialize a potential cancer treatment worldwide.
Zhu taught immunology and microbiology at West China University of Medical Sciences before striking out on his own.
forbes_facts: Zhu has a master's in biology from Fudan University and a doctorate in management from Sichuan University.

name: Ty Warner
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2001-2025); Hurun Global (2014-2026); Wikidata (2025)
forbes_bio: Ty Warner is the creator of Beanie Babies, the plush toy fad of the 1990s.
Warner used the profits from selling Beanie Babies to assemble a high-end hotel portfolio, including the Four Seasons in New York.
Ty Inc. still sells Beanie Babies but has expanded its offerings to include toys like Beanie Boos and Beanie Bellies.
His Las Ventanas al Paraiso resort in Mexico rents its Ty Warner Mansion for $35,000 a night.
Warner has donated $100 million in cash and toys to the Children's Hunger Fund since 2005.
forbes_facts: A onetime bellman, car valet and fruit market vendor, Warner found his calling as a salesman, peddling encyclopedias and later stuffed animals at toymaker Dakin.
Warner was convicted of tax evasion and paid a $53 million fine in 2013 for stashing money in a Swiss bank, but avoided jail time.
Zach Galifianakis played Warner in the 2023 fictionalized drama film "The Beanie Bubble."

name: Yitzhak Tshuva
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2001-2025); Hurun Global (2014-2026)
forbes_bio: Yitzhak Tshuva made his billions in energy and real estate.
His private El Ad Group, a real estate firm, has developments in Manhattan, Florida, Louisiana, Montreal and Israel.
His is also the controlling shareholder of Delek Group, a publicly-traded conglomerate with interests in automotives, oil and gas.
His family immigrated from Libya to Israel when he was six months old. He later served in the Israeli army and worked in Israel's Ministry of Defense.

name: Otto Boehringer
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2025); Hurun Global (2026)
forbes_bio: Otto Boehringer derives his fortune from Germany's Boehringer Ingelheim, the world's largest privately-owned pharmaceutical company.
Now in its fifth generation, Boehringer Ingelheim was founded in 1885 but traces its entrepreneurial roots back to 1817.
The company grew by selling ingredients to pharmacies, textile merchants and the food industry and had a workforce of 1,500 by 1939.
Today it employs 53,000 and boasts a presence in 130 markets.
Otto along with 14 members of the family own equal parts of the company.

name: Barry Diller
sec_insider_companies: Expedia Group, Inc. (EXPE) - Chairman & Sr. Executive; IAC Inc. (IAC) - Chairman & Senior Executive
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2001-2025); Hurun Global (2014-2026); Wikidata (2017); SEC insider holdings (2026)
forbes_bio: Barry Diller founded internet and media conglomerate People Incorporated (formerly IAC) in 1995. He remains senior executive and chairman.
The public company owns the print and digital publisher People Inc., The Daily Beast and equity stakes in companies such as MGM Resorts International, Turo and healthcare jobs site Vivian Health.
Diller is also chairman and senior executive of online travel giant Expedia, which acquired its holding company, Liberty Expedia, in a $2.6 billion deal in 2019.
Prior to founding People Incorporated, he worked at ABC, Paramount and Fox and oversaw launches of hit TV shows including "Cheers" and "The Simpsons."
He built Pier 55 -- named "Little Island" -- a park and performance venue in the Hudson River that opened in 2021.
He is married to designer Diane Von Furstenberg and owns an estimated third of her eponymous fashion company.
forbes_facts: Diller never graduated from college and got a job in the mail room at William Morris talent agency.
Diller is the owner of the EOS yacht, one of the largest private sailing yachts in the world.

name: Martin Haefner
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2013-2025); Hurun Global (2014-2026)
forbes_bio: Martin Haefner's fortune largely stems from his former stake in IT management software maker CA Technologies, acquired by Broadcom in July 2018.
He inherited half of his father Walter's stake in CA Technologies when he died in June 2012, then the world's oldest billionaire at 101.
He also inherited part of car dealer AMAG, which sells brands including Volkswagen, Audi, Bentley and Porsche.
His sister, Eva Maria Bucher-Haefner, inherited equal stakes in CA Technologies and AMAG. He bought her stake in AMAG in 2018.
Martin co-owns the Bellerive Hotel in Lausanne, Switzerland, with his sister.
forbes_facts: Prior to joining the family business, Haefner taught math in Baden and Lucerne, Switzerland.

name: Xu Shihui
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2001-2025); Hurun Global (2014-2026); Hurun China (2007-2026)
forbes_bio: Xu Shihui is the chairman of Chinese snack and beverage maker Dali Foods Group.
Xu started out in the cookie business and took the food empire public in 2015. Today it is best known for its Copico potato chips, Heqizheng herbal tea and Haochidian soda crackers.
Citing reasons including unsatisfactory share performance, Xu took Hong Kong-listed Dali private in 2023 in a deal that values it at $6.6 billion.
His daughter Xu Yangyang rose from Dali's vice president to its president in 2025.
forbes_facts: Xu works seven days a week and hopes his work style inspires other managers. (He met Forbes Asia in his office in 2016 during a national holiday.)
Xu is the son of a laborer who worked at Dali when it was a collective and amassed shares by turning the business around.
